units.name: hide_oam_sprites
units.summary: Write F0 to every sprite Y byte in the 256-byte OAM shadow, eight sprites per iteration. Tile, attribute and X bytes are retained; offscreen Y hides the old sprites.

units.name: dispatch_vblank_video_work
units.summary: A pending scroll update sends the prepared attribute/tile buffers to the PPU, then proceeds to shared OAM/scroll finalization. Otherwise perform palette/fade or chapter-specific pattern animation. This bank must be mapped when the NMI calls it.

units.name: upload_scroll_attributes
units.summary: Reset the PPU address latch. Upload eight attribute bytes at low-address strides of eight, then two horizontal groups of eight bytes to paired nametables. The small B906 helper restarts an attribute row when an eight-bit increment wraps. The unknown three-byte gaps at wrap paths remain opaque; they are not silently decoded here.

units.name: upload_vertical_tile_strip
units.summary: Select PPU increment 32 and upload the thirty-byte prepared tile column. The split index chooses when to reset the PPU address for the second part of the wrapped column. If all thirty bytes fit in the first part, skip the second address setup.

units.name: upload_horizontal_tile_strips
units.summary: Select PPU increment one. Write 32 prepared tile bytes to one nametable, toggle nametable bit 2 in the high address, then write another 32. The unrolled stores preserve the exact NMI timing and buffer order.

units.name: upload_palette_for_fade
units.summary: When fade work is active, write a sixteen-color chapter palette through the current color mask. Palette selector six uses 32 colors; other selectors append the common sixteen-color sprite palette. FF entries bypass the mask. This is bit masking of color values, not arithmetic luminance interpolation.

units.name: finish_video_frame
units.summary: Hide the sprite at the current OAM cursor and DMA page 02. Restore PPU control, horizontal/vertical scroll and mask shadows. Every fourth frame move the palette color mask toward black or toward 3F, then clear the scroll-update request and increment both frame counters. Cursor zero is also a valid first sprite index; the caller handles full-buffer cases separately.

units.name: measure_object_visibility
units.summary: Restore object Y from the active slot. Compute screen coordinates by subtracting the camera from 16-bit world positions. Measure overflow beyond the horizontal screen and the vertical 0..EF interval in rounded 16-pixel units; sum the two distances. Zero keeps visible bit 1 set; a nonzero distance clears it. If the distance reaches the object threshold, select state 18 unless the secondary-flag/timer exception retains it.

units.name: connected_1c763
units.summary: Object state-entry timer transfer, movement/spawn cycle, request preparation, delay drain and Y oscillator.

units.name: transfer_contact_timer_parameter
units.summary: Negative animation-cache status transfers the saved motion value into the timer, clears it, and decrements a nonzero parameter. Nonnegative animation-cache status copies the timer back to that motion field.

units.name: advance_motion_and_spawn_phase
units.summary: Select animation 0. Without primary bit 4 restore stored vertical speed while the parameter is zero. With it, flip the X coordinate low bit, compare against the player and queue a type 4 request. A running parameter counts down and clears response 40 once all velocity components are zero.

units.name: emit_secondary_flag_request
units.summary: Clear response 40 after all velocity components stop. Secondary bit 2 queues the field-selected request at the current position and chooses animation 1 A.

units.name: select_parameter_animation_and_flags
units.summary: Nonzero parameter selects animation parameter+8 and enables paired response flags; zero clears the secondary flag and selects animation E.

units.name: drain_parameter_and_oscillate_y
units.summary: A negative animation cache writes 40 hexadecimal to the first slot of the anchor-low array without indexing. If the current slot anchor-low byte is zero, initialize its acceleration parameter, distance threshold and blink parameter. Otherwise subtract parameter low bits with saturation; a value below 20 hexadecimal toggles the X low bit. Clear parameter low bits, convert Y to cells and reverse vertical speed at the saved cell boundaries.

units.name: integrate_object_motion
units.summary: Save previous 24-bit Y and X positions. Add signed vertical acceleration derived from the object parameter (scaled by flag bit 2), cap positive vertical speed, then integrate velocity with sign extension. For X, either combine the base signed speed with an external velocity or approach that target by a bounded acceleration; set contact bit 3 on reaching it. Clear one-frame impulses/contact bits and integrate the 24-bit X position. Unless wrapping is permitted, reject X high bytes outside 0..7 and restore the previous X position.

regions.summary: Object input-mask selection, speed restoration/reversal, facing comparison, collision response and shared continuation tails.

units.name: connected_1cc4c
units.summary: Object input-mask selection, speed restoration/reversal, facing comparison, collision response and shared continuation tails.

units.name: stop_horizontal_then_continue
units.summary: Reset horizontal motion and tail-call the shared object continuation.

units.name: restore_base_speed_then_continue
units.summary: Restore the type-defined base horizontal speed and tail-call the shared object continuation.

units.name: prepare_simple_response_masks
units.summary: Initialize input/response masks for the shared directional test. The scratch bytes are per-call masks, not persistent object fields.

units.name: prepare_directional_response_masks
units.summary: Choose one of two mask sets from response sign, then test primary flags and the collision/input field. Select animation 1 or 4 on the blocked paths; otherwise restore base speed and continue. Facing toggles share the speed-reset entry.

units.name: toggle_object_facing_and_stop_x
units.summary: Toggle primary facing bit 0 and tail-call horizontal speed reset.

units.name: countdown_and_reverse_vertical_motion
units.summary: Test facing-relative response bits and primary flags. Decrement timer on the free path; choose animation 3 or 4 as needed. After restoring base speed, conditionally negate its two-byte representation before the shared continuation.

units.name: stop_base_speed_before_object_tail
units.summary: Clear the base horizontal speed and enter the shared object tail. The next independent entry selects facing and prepares doubled speed.

units.name: face_player_and_prepare_doubled_base_speed
units.summary: Face the selected player using coarse X comparison. Special primary flags stop base speed or select animation 4; otherwise double the stored two-byte type speed into base horizontal motion, then continue.

units.name: face_player_and_restore_speed
units.summary: Set facing toward the player. Primary flags may stop movement or select animation 4; otherwise restore the stored two-byte speed, with timer/frame changes on the flagged path.

units.name: quadruple_saved_horizontal_speed
units.summary: A primary sign flag takes the shared stop path. Otherwise multiply the stored two-byte speed by four into horizontal velocity and continue.

units.name: toggle_primary_motion_flag
units.summary: Toggle primary bit 20 and continue through the common object tail.

units.name: start_upward_object_motion
units.summary: Set primary bit 8, clear one velocity component and saved motion, set vertical speed to -6 and distance threshold 2, then continue.

units.name: respond_to_facing_collision
units.summary: Select the facing-specific response bit. A collision selects animation 4 and toggles facing; otherwise restore type-defined base speed and continue, with response bit 4 controlling the shared tail.

phase1.evidence: Accepted fetch after recorded natural/artificial gameplay, exact immutable decode and effective banks. Evidence analysis/round01/expansion-evidence.json and rpc-live.jsonl.

regions.summary: Readability reviewed in object_turning_motion. Supported mechanics, control-flow names and shared operands are explained in source.

units.name: object_turning_motion
units.summary: On first entry, retain the initial X anchor and initialize speed. Compare current X with the anchor; when the side changes relative to auxiliary bit 6, toggle primary facing bit zero and update that side flag. Derive signed vertical velocity from the difference between base speed and absolute horizontal velocity, then enter animation update.

units.name: reset_object_slot
units.summary: Mark type/state, distance, replacement score and animation-state cache FF. Clear flags, movement, timers, animation indexes and contact accumulators for slot Y. Array bases are spaced by five because there are five slots; fields are separate arrays, not an interleaved struct.

units.name: bounce_object_moving_left

units.name: apply_object_slope_height

units.name: mark_unsettled_object_slope_contact

units.name: apply_horizontal_object_slope_sample
units.summary: Mark auxiliary08, compare Y cell fraction with the computed slope height and snap only when the surface has been reached. Clear external X motion after snapping.

units.name: align_object_slope_to_right_edge
units.summary: Use cell fraction 0F for the shared edge alignment.

units.name: align_object_slope_to_left_edge
units.summary: Use cell fraction zero for the shared edge alignment.

units.name: align_object_slope_edge
units.summary: Upward speed uses ordinary bounce. Otherwise move Y two pixels above its coarse cell edge, set X to the selected edge and Y fraction to FF. Vertical contact also runs D275, stops Y motion and starts timer C0; horizontal contact returns.

units.name: ignore_object_tile_response

units.name: bounce_object_and_push_right
units.summary: Apply the shared surface bounce, then install external horizontal speed +1 with zero fraction.

units.name: bounce_object_with_long_timer
units.summary: Companion surface response uses timer B0 on downward impact. The upward displacement uses the complemented low nibble. Horizontal cases mirror the same signed wall-bounce and slope-edge choices as D2A8.

units.name: snap_object_to_alternate_y_edge
units.summary: Advance Y using the complemented difference from the sampled edge, clear Y fraction and set upward FFFF speed/contact10.

units.name: bounce_object_from_opposite_wall

units.name: set_object_vertical_impulse_on_left_contact
units.summary: Mirror the preceding horizontal-direction test; vertical contact still selects signed Y speed magnitude eight.

units.name: stop_falling_object_or_push_horizontally

units.name: stop_rising_object_or_push_horizontally

units.name: apply_negative_crossing_impulses
units.summary: Mark contact and choose vertical or external-horizontal impulses from axis, velocity sign and cell crossing. Contact bit02 distinguishes the special crossed-cell case. Magnitudes are +8 or -8; these are integer velocity components, not coordinates.

units.name: apply_negative_motion_impulses

units.name: apply_positive_crossing_impulses
units.summary: Mirror the earlier crossing family with positive external X on downward crossing. Vertical rising speed becomes -8 and clears its fraction; horizontal crossing and contact02 choose Y versus signed external X impulses.

units.name: apply_positive_motion_impulses
units.summary: Companion sign family marks contact and transfers positive external X on upward vertical motion. Horizontal crossing checks choose +8 Y or signed external X; zero the relevant fractional components on transfer.

units.name: mark_object_response_after_y_crossing

units.summary: Integrate object motion, reject excluded or out-of-range vertical states, and compute map pointers from previous/current positions. When an axis changes, translate map-cell IDs through the collision table and dispatch the class-specific response. Gather eight surrounding property bits into the object tile-contact mask using the bank-six property lookup. Return with bank six selected. One horizontal continuation remains unknown; the source notes that boundary rather than inventing it.

units.name: compute_object_map_pointer
units.summary: Two entries choose previous or current X. Divide 16-bit X/Y coordinates by sixteen to get coarse cells, using the upper edge when moving upward unless the object has the special primary flag. Build the cell address as map base + coarse X + coarse Y*128. Store coarse coordinates for comparisons with players and return the read pointer in scratch 27/28.

units.summary: Negative stream bytes enter here: the high nibble selects an indirect audio command and the low nibble is its argument. The shared audio_fetch_next_event entry reads and advances the voice stream. Nonnegative bytes encode pitch class and octave/duration modifiers. Special noise/DMC voices trigger fixed hardware effects; pitched voices derive a timer from lookup tables and octave shifts. A rest disables or mutes the relevant channel. Packed stream bytes are data, not CPU instructions.

units.summary: Command FF clears APU registers and installs default pulse/triangle/noise control values and enable mask 07. Commands below six write a two-byte period from zero page X into a selected channel. Seven disables noise while preserving DMC-active state; 08..10 configure pulse control/sweep; 14..16 clear channel periods. Other command values pass through explicit returns. The final 17 case contains an apparently unsatisfiable comparison; preserve its exact mechanics rather than claiming a reachable feature.

units.summary: Player floor/input response: mode reset, tile exceptions, movement lock, phase cadence and upward motion alternatives.

units.name: apply_player_floor_response
units.summary: Run the shared floor check. Input bit 0 resets mode flags and horizontal accumulator; tile types 4/5 retain the alternate response bit. Stop vertical motion for idle/blocked states, preserve the old mode on the stack across the shared test, and flip facing on an eight-phase cadence when movement input remains. Alternate input 40 chooses upward speed -7 instead of -2, both with fraction 1.

units.name: align_player_coordinates_to_cell

units.name: start_opposite_facing_cell_response

units.name: apply_player_vertical_rebound
units.summary: Run the shared contact-frame helper. Nonnegative vertical speed clears horizontal speed and directional input; high input bits choose rebound magnitude 3 or 6. units.name: render_sprite_requests_to_oam
units.summary: Snapshot frame parity and request count, select bank six, then visit three-byte sprite requests forward or backward on alternate frames to vary priority. Look up the frame layout pointer and dimensions, derive top-left coordinates and tile bias, and clip sprites crossing screen edges. Layout records are Y offset, tile index, attribute, X offset terminated by FF. Fill the OAM shadow until the cursor wraps, then process bank-four auxiliary sprites and restore bank six. Three clipped-copy continuations use their independently checked source, cursor and clipping contracts.

units.name: select_prg_bank_a
units.summary: Entry F48B saves A but uses that same value as the mapper bank. The shared F48C tail saves X, records the selected bank, writes to a bank-indexed ROM address, restores X and the saved A, then returns. The mapper register value is a 16-KiB selector; it is not an effective 8-KiB physical bank index.

units.name: gameplay_frame_loop
units.summary: Choose chapter music, enable NMI/rendering and wait for a fresh frame. Build player state and scroll buffers; clear OAM; when unpaused, scan spawn edges and update five objects. Render requests, draw player status/check pause when permitted, read controllers, and wait for the next frame. The wait returns whether it actually spun; the pause/state byte uses that result to request state two before continuing.

units.name: show_resource_screen_and_wait
units.summary: Save resource selector and chapter, temporarily select chapter six for pattern setup, disable NMI and resolve the resource stream pointer. Interpret its PPU command stream, optionally draw the continue-count tile, then enable rendering, fade in and wait for A/Start across both controllers. Wait for release and finally for all input zero, preventing carry-through. Chapter five returns directly; other screens disable rendering before return. The special continue selection loop can return after release or remove two return bytes before restarting chapter selection.

regions.summary: Wait a frame, poll bank-six controllers and draw the selection marker at work21+5F. Direction bits choose the two marker positions. units.name: poll_continue_screen_selection

units.name: discard_screen_caller_and_restart

units.name: wait_for_screen_confirm_release
units.summary: Continue frame/controller polling until A/Start is released, then tail-call FF9A so its RTS returns to the original screen caller.

Zero ends; one consumes a big-endian PPU address; two consumes a fill tile adjusted by 86 and invokes nametable clear. Other bytes emit tile value byte+66 to PPUDATA. units.name: prepare_scroll_buffers
units.summary: Reduce camera Y modulo 240 while counting nametable rows, derive pixel scroll, tile/coarse coordinates and map/attribute source pointers. Retain horizontal nametable parity and compare current tile coordinates with previous ones. On tile movement, calculate attribute destinations, build the vertical and horizontal buffers, and set the NMI update request. A forced camera refresh decrements its marker but does not invent a tile-boundary movement.

units.summary: Compare the last consumed animation counter with the NMI counter until they differ, then save the new value. X is zero if a fresh frame was already available and FF if the routine had to spin. Callers use this distinction in pause/state scheduling.

units.name: nmi_video_and_sound
units.summary: Save A/X/Y and the selected UxROM bank. Switch to bank five for vblank video work, bank six for rate-controlled music, then tick the sound-effect voice twice. Restore the interrupted bank and registers before RTI. The bank-selection helper scratch is safe here only through this explicit save/restore protocol.

units.name: decompress_chapter_graphics
units.summary: Synchronize to vblank, select chapter source/end pointers and resource bank, then set PPU destination 1000. Chapters five and above use a raw page copy. Other chapters parse commands until source reaches the exclusive end: bit 6 selects a literal run, bit 7 selects a seven-bit mask packet, and neither selects an alternating-value repeat. Low-six-bit literal count is decremented modulo 256 exactly as encoded; zero is not silently normalized.

units.name: emit_graphics_alternating_run
units.summary: Swap A and the remembered value on each output and decrement the sixteen-bit count until zero, then fetch the next command. The remembered value intentionally survives packets; clearing it here would change decompression.

units.name: decode_graphics_mask_packet
units.summary: Shift the command into a seven-decision mask. Read a candidate byte into the remembered value; each mask bit either consumes a literal stream byte or reuses one of the two alternating remembered values. Emit exactly seven bytes, preserving the original swaps and carry flow, then return to command parsing.

units.name: draw_title_and_mode_menu
units.summary: Wait for vblank, disable NMI and upload fixed-bank-six title tiles plus a bank-zero mapped tile block and attribute bytes. Enable rendering and seed three or four sprite requests according to player/mode selection. Each frame hides OAM, renders requests, reads controllers and waits. Select toggles the mode/player combination; A/Start confirms only after release. Finish by clearing request/cursor state and tail-calling bank-five OAM initialization.
